shared_structure: flower and sticky insect-trapping leaf system
study_design: regional survey plus local interference experiment across abiotic contexts
notes: Direct pollinator-prey conflict: small pollinators are trapped and their loss depletes the resource limiting reproduction; interference is environment dependent.

study_design: sympatric comparative field study plus flower-height manipulation
notes: Short-raceme species shared pollinators with D. pauciflora but no pollinators were found in traps; long scapes were not supported as pollinator-protection adaptations.

shared_structure: flower and basal sticky-trap display system
study_design: sympatric comparative field study plus flower-height manipulation
notes: Long scape creates large flower-trap distance, yet no pollinators were captured and height mainly increased pollinator visitation; separation is observed but conflict mechanism is not demonstrated.

shared_structure: flower/trap visual and spatial signalling system
study_design: flower-visitor and prey sampling plus behavioural colour and separation experiments
notes: Large flower-trap distance and white floral display reduce pollinator entrapment; study demonstrates separation mechanism rather than a realized fitness conflict.

shared_structure: flower/trap visual and spatial signalling system
study_design: flower-visitor and prey sampling plus behavioural colour and separation experiments
notes: Spatial separation and floral colour are consistent with pollinator sparing, while direct fitness loss from pollinator capture is not demonstrated.

shared_structure: adjacent flowers and sticky traps with distinct volatile signals
study_design: flower/trap volatile chemistry plus behavioural attraction assays
notes: Flowers and traps are spatially adjacent, but distinct odour blends partition attraction: floral odour attracts flower visitors while trap odour attracts prey. Fitness-level conflict remains unresolved.

shared_structure: short flower-trap separation in a selfing sundew
study_design: field pollinator/prey census plus flower-removal experiment
notes: Four of five major pollinator species were also caught as prey, but autonomous selfing may buffer reproductive cost; ecological overlap is high without a demonstrated fitness conflict.

shared_structure: short flower-trap separation in a selfing sundew
study_design: field pollinator/prey census plus flower-removal experiment
notes: One of six major pollinator species was trapped; selfing and pollinator behaviour can buffer costs, so capture overlap is not promoted to positive fitness conflict.

shared_structure: flower and snap-trap arthropod interaction system
study_design: field flower-visitor pollen-load survey and trap-prey community comparison
notes: Flower visitors and trap prey show near-zero niche overlap; spatial separation of flowers and traps may contribute to partitioning, but realized conflict is rare.

shared_structure: flowers produced close to sticky trap leaves
study_design: 2007-2021 field video hand-pollination prey census and flower-removal experiment
notes: Pollinators comprised 57% of identified prey and flowers facilitate capture; female fitness is buffered by high autofertility, making this a direct conflict with asymmetric fitness consequences.
